name: memfd-then-execveat
why: memfd_create followed by execveat in the SAME pid within 10s is the fileless-execution correlation. The atomic open()s the payload first (fd 3), so the memfd is fd 4 (memfd_create exit=4, execveat a0=4). auditd logs execveat at syscall exit, AFTER the image is replaced, so that record carries the NEW image's comm 'memfd:atomic' and exe '/memfd:atomic (deleted)', not the pre-exec deteng_ values
source: recorded: strace+live run of memfd_exec_behavioral.c on this host -- memfd_create("atomic",0)=4, execveat(4,"",...,AT_EMPTY_PATH), post-exec comm=memfd:atomic exe=/memfd:atomic (deleted). (On older kernels the comm is the fd number, e.g. '6', as the benign slice has for runc.)

name: memfd-then-execveat-window-edge
why: the same pair 9s apart stays inside the 10s window; the correlation must still fire at the window edge. This dropper creates the memfd as its first fd (fd 3, a1=MFD_CLOEXEC), then fexecve's it; the execveat record carries the post-exec image (comm 'memfd:payload', exe '/memfd:payload (deleted)')
source: synthetic: a slower dropper, memfd_create and execveat 9s apart in one pid

name: memfd-create-only
why: a process that creates an anonymous memfd but never execs it (common for shared-memory buffers) is half the correlation; the execveat base must be required
source: synthetic: memfd_create used as a sealed shared-memory buffer, no exec

name: execveat-only
why: execveat of a real on-disk fd (fexecve of an O_PATH descriptor) with no preceding memfd_create is the other half; the memfd_create base must be required
source: synthetic: a launcher using fexecve on a normal file descriptor

name: memfd-and-execveat-different-pid
why: memfd_create in a parent and execveat in a forked child split the two syscalls across pids: the documented fork-variant coverage gap, which the pid group-by must enforce (mirrors controls/memfd_fexecve_in_child.c)
source: synthetic: memfd_create in pid X, fexecve in forked child pid Y, within 10s

name: memfd-then-execveat-too-late
why: the same pid does memfd_create and execveat but 20s apart, outside the 10s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: memfd_create and execveat in one pid, 20s apart
